description: We're a team of five working on the Earth Systems and Trends challenge!
summary: BoundaryWatch lets anyone explore how air moves above U.S. cities, what it carries, and how that connects to the vegetation below. It takes in a total of 41 variables relating to air quality metrics, atmospheric measurements and vegetation data to see how they affect each other. It also performs statistical tests to assess whether or not these relationships and trends are deemed significant. This is important as it catalogues various data types into a single interactive web page easily accessible by anybody, and connects atmospheric physics to ecology, allowing for better environmental research.
details: BoundaryWatch is an interactive Earth observation dashboard. It allows anyone to investigate how the lowest layer of the atmosphere (the planetary boundary layer) traps or disperses air pollutants, and how that pollution impacts plant health across 19 U.S. cities and landscapes. By automatically aggregating and standardizing 41 live weather, air quality, and satellite vegetation variables from Meteomatics and NASA MODIS (via the Microsoft Planetary Computer) onto a common yearly timeline from 2016 to 2025, the platform eliminates hours of manual data preparation to aid environmental systems research. Javascript was used for the web page, and our team had to decide which types of data we wanted to compare, which required creativity and analytical thinking.
